sn12.40:1.4: This enigmatic saying is also at [ud8.4:3.4](), [mn144:11.6](), and [sn35.87:11.6](). | “Inclination” is _nati_, from a root meaning “to bend”. Sometimes used in the sense of a “inclination of mind” ([mn19:6.1]()), here, as the following lines make clear, it refers to the mind inclining to rebirth; explained by the commentary as “craving”. Compare the English idiom, “one is bent on destruction”.
